records.prompt: Use case: style-transfer. Asset type: RTS cutout sprite sheet. Image 1 is the edit target and determines the objects, historical architecture and layout. Image 2 is the drawing-style reference only. Redraw image 1 in the same print family as image 2. Vietnamese Đông Hồ folk woodblock drawing language: large flat opaque pigment shapes, decisive slightly uneven warm-black carved contours, sparse decorative curved marks. Vermilion, ochre, indigo, leaf green and warm black. Eliminate gradients, realistic modelling, tiny engraving hatch, microtexture and hundreds of individual roof tiles. Interior detail must be much sparser than the silhouette. No glow, drop shadow or sepia filter. Keep all ten original structures in exact grid order. Preserve roof type and tier count, distinctive gates, entrances and compound footprints. Use broad roof pigment shapes and a few clear tile or thatch marks. Keep existing front-centred orthographic elevated camera with horizontal eaves; do not change to isometric. No people, terrain, earth platforms, scenery, shadows or paper under the buildings; courtyard holes stay transparent. Landscape 1536×1024, 4 columns and 3 rows. Row1: thatched house, tiled house, communal hall, pagoda tower. Row2: original gate-and-fence enclosure, original wall enclosure, bamboo hedge, kitchen. Row3: buffalo byre, round grain bin, empty, empty. Keep at least 24 pixels of transparent margin around every complete silhouette and wide gutters. Roof tips must not touch cell boundaries. No labels, text or grid lines. GENUINE transparent alpha including holes and courtyards, not a painted checkerboard. No paper background.
